history.p: The Sanctus was performed in Neukirche in February 1732, that is while Scheibe was still living in Leipzig. It is possible that the work might have been commissioned by the church organist and cantor Carl Gotthelf Gerlach. Following Gerlach’s death in 1761, the work was obtained by Breitkopf and included as one of their house manuscripts; in 1761 and 1769 it was listed in the publisher’s sales catalogues. At the end of the eighteenth century, the Sanctus was acquired by O.K.F. von Voß-Buch together with other of Scheibe’s church music with Latin text.

physDesc.physMedium: Eleven instrumental and vocal parts in original grey-blue O.K.F. von Voß-Buch limp folder on which '288. part.' has been added in upper right-hand corner. Source includes three distinct hands of which one might be Scheibe (copyist C; ob.1, 2). All vocal parts, strings and continuo are in the same hand (copyist A), while the org. is in a different one (copyist B).
